{{Quote|Friend, you've helped me so much today, I greatly appreciate it. I can't begin to thank you for your help. You're the type of person who reminds me why we fight against the Empire.|translated=1|Nien Nunb in [[Sullustese/Legends|Sullustese]]|<ref name="Squadrons Over Corellia">{{SWGTCG|set=Squadrons Over Corellia|cardname=Nien Nunb}}</ref>}}
'''Nien Nunb''' was a male [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]] [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]].<ref name="Jedi Knights TCG - Masters of the Force">''[[Jedi Knights Trading Card Game]]''</ref> He grew up in the caves of his homeworld, [[Sullust/Legends|Sullust]], with his sister, [[Aril Nunb]]. Later, he worked for the [[SoroSuub Corporation/Legends|SoroSuub Corporation]] as a smuggler. During one of his smuggling flights, he befriended [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]]&mdash;an individual Nunb would have great deals with in later years. It was with Calrissian that he would copilot the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] during the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]. He went on to become the administrator of the [[Kessel/Legends|Kessel]] [[Spice/Legends|spice]] mines, and sporadically worked with the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] and its successor, the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]].

==Biography==
===Early life===
{{Quote|Don't worry. My friend's down there. He'll have that shield down on time. Or this'll be the shortest offensive of all time.|[[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] to Nien Nunb|<ref name="Episode 6">{{Film|VI}}</ref>}}
[[File:Nien_Nunb_JKTCG.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Nien Nunb.]]
In his youth, Nien Nunb became acquainted with [[Sian Tevv/Legends|Sian Tevv]], a fellow [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]] whose parents regarded Nunb as an unseemly individual and disapproved of his relationship with Tevv. The talented and ambitious Nunb formed a lasting friendship with Tevv, but they eventually went their separate ways, with Nunb mastering the skills necessary to be a [[Spacer/Legends|spacer]] while Tevv studied to become a [[Diplomat/Legends|diplomat]]. Nunb achieved success in his field, entering a legitimate career as one of the top cargo runners of the [[SoroSuub Corporation/Legends|SoroSuub Corporation]],<ref name="LCSB:Tevv" /> for which he transported minerals and other raw materials to outlying [[Star system/Legends|systems]]. The speed of Nunb's [[Starship/Legends|ship]] and the quality of his work earned him substantial pay and appreciation from his employer, but when SoroSuub chose to support the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and subsequently take control of the [[Sullust system/Legends|Sullust system]] from its people, Nunb quit the career; in the process, he faced [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] fire and hostile company [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]].<ref name="GG5:Nunb">[[Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 5: Return of the Jedi'', Second Edition]] {{C|Under ''Nien Nunb''}}</ref>

After some soul-searching, Nunb decided to use his skills&mdash;acquired through years of [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggling]]&mdash;to undermine the SoroSuub Corporation. He began stealing SoroSuub consignments from the company and shipping them to the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebellion]]; as he hoped to inspire his people and rouse them to action, he committed these acts publicly and with bravado. Others soon began to join Nunb in his efforts, and he and his band of smugglers and outlaws became folk heroes to the Sullustan people. [[Sian Tevv/Legends|Sian Tevv]], now a famous [[Politics/Legends|political]] agitator, provided quiet support to Nunb. SoroSuub established the [[Sullustan Home Guard/Legends|Home Guard]] with the goal of defending Sullust and stopping Nunb, and while the Guard virtually eliminated [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] attacks by outsiders, it was less successful in operations against Nunb's gang and other Sullustans.<ref name="GG5:Nunb" />

===Galactic Civil War===
Nunb decided that joining the Rebel Alliance and directly fighting the Empire was the only way to affect change, and his gang soon became affiliated with the Alliance, although an Imperial [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]] destroyed their ships while they were attempting to establish contact with the Rebels. SoroSuub later allied with the Alliance as well, offering the Sullust system as a secret staging area for the Rebel [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|fleet]], and Nunb was hailed as a hero of his people upon this reversal in policy.<ref name="GG5:Nunb" />

Nunb was chosen especially by [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian]] to co-pilot the [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']] during the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]].<ref name="Jedi Knights TCG - Masters of the Force" /> Nunb was also instrumental in the Alliance's discovery that the Endor shield generator was still activated: while discussing their inability to get a reading on the [[Death Star II/Legends|Second Death Star's]] shield status, Nunb posited the theory that the Empire was jamming them, causing Calrissian to realize mid-response that the Empire had anticipated their arrival. Later in the battle, as the ''Falcon'' entered the Death Star's superstructure, Nunb reminded Calrissian of the correct [[Concussion missile/Legends|concussion missile]] launch code, allowing the [[General/Legends|general]] to fire on and destroy the immense [[Space station/Legends|space station's]] [[Reactor/Legends|reactor core]].<ref name="Vandelhelm">{{Wizards|url=default.asp?x=starwars/article/sw20040304vandelhelm|text=Vandelhelm: Enemies and Alloys|int=Vandelhelm: Enemies and Alloys}}</ref> As such, he was awarded the [[Kalidor Crescent/Legends|Kalidor Crescent]] for his heroism in participating in the destruction of the Second Death Star. Sometime after Endor, Nunb was again part of the ''Falcon''{{'s}} crew, this time as the co-pilot of [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]]. Though Nunb had piloted Solo's starship in wild maneuvers through the shipyards of [[Fondor/Legends|Fondor]], Han could not be convinced by Calrissian to accept Nunb as a temporary substitute for [[Chewbacca/Legends|Chewbacca]], who was spending time with his family on [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]]. Though suspicious about Nunb's qualities, Han's respect for the Sullustan grew during their [[Mission to Vandelhelm|mission]] to rescue the [[Venerated Ones]] of [[Vandelhelm/Legends|Vandelhelm]], where he even saved Han's life from a [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtrooper]] attack,<ref name="SW98">[[Star Wars (1977) 98|''Star Wars'' (1977) 98]]</ref> although this development was not reciprocated in Nunb's regard for Solo.<ref name="Vandelhelm" />

[[File:Nien_Nunb_-_SWGTCG.jpg|thumb|Nien Nunb as a pilot.]]
In [[13 ABY/Legends|13 ABY]], Calrissian purchased the [[Spice/Legends|spice]] mines of [[Kessel/Legends|Kessel]] and installed Nunb as administrator. The Sullustan managed to dramatically increase the planet's standards by replacing unwilling slave labor with employed species, that like his own people, preferred living underground.<ref name="Crisis at Crystal Reef">''[[Young Jedi Knights: Crisis at Crystal Reef]]''</ref> In the same year he assisted Calrissian once more as co-pilot in the Battle of [[Nam Chorios/Legends|Nam Chorios]] during the [[Death Seed]] crisis.

[[14 ABY/Legends|The following year]], Nunb returned to Vandelhelm with Solo in the ''Falcon'' for the launch of the [[Solo-class combat freighter|''Solo''-class combat freighter]] in a ceremony celebrating the tenth anniversary of the Vandelhelm mission. While there, Nien again saved the life of Solo, as well as that of Venerated One and [[Metalsmiths Guild|Metalsmiths]] [[Guild Master/Legends|Guildmistress]] [[Lillindri Nanimei Filda Vandelhelm XXXII]], pushing them clear of a rogue [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] before grappling the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] and discharging its own blaster into its neck. The droid had been directed by the Guildmistress' brother and fellow Venerated One, [[Endrodanar Tiopuld Shaamador Vandelhelm XXIV]] to assassinate his sister, allowing him to take control of Vandelhelm, while pinning the killing on Nien Nunb as a terrorist act in the name of "Sullustan rights".<ref name="Vandelhelm" />

===Later life===
In [[24 ABY/Legends|24 ABY]], [[Torvon]], a member of [[Black Sun/Legends|Black Sun]] acting as Nunb's [[Second Administrator]] tried to murder Nunb on Kessel, but the Sullustan administrator survived the assassination attempt. When the mines were overtaken by [[Czethros]], leader of Black Sun, Nunb allied with [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]] and [[Lowbacca]] to regain control.<ref name="Crisis at Crystal Reef" />

It is said that Nunb was still administrator of Kessel during the war against the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] and that he highly increased the planet's defensive systems to hold off the invaders.

Sometime before [[43 ABY]], he gained a partner's share of the Kessel mines along with Calrissian and his wife Tendra, and helped destroy the subterranean tunnels of Kessel to save the planet from breaking apart from ground quakes.

During 43.5 ABY, Nunb was known to have been a co-owner and manager of of one of Kessel's most prominent mineworks. He was contacted by [[Ben Skywalker]] during their search for [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] [[Sith apprentice/Legends|apprentice]] [[Vestara Khai]]. Nunb informed Ben that a [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] Khai had landed and refueled on Kessel without paying, and had acquired a galactic map update for her ship. He also informed him of the ship's name, [[Bright Sun|''She's a Chancer'']].

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|He has a very likable look with those big, black eyes and big stuck-out ears - he kind of reminded me a little bit of Dopey from ''Snow White''.|[[Mike Quinn]] on Nien Nunb|<ref name="In the Star Wars Universe">{{InsiderCite|47|In the Star Wars Universe|In the ''Star Wars'' Universe: Mike Quinn}}</ref>}}
[[File:NienNunb-NEGTC.png|thumb|right|150px|Nien Nunb.]]
The character Nien Nunb was realized as a puppet for his appearance in [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']]. He was performed by [[Mike Quinn]] and [[Richard Bonehill]]. Quinn operated Nunb's face, which was a large animatronic hand puppet, and Bonehill was the extra wearing the full body suit.

The name refers to the fact that the character was "Number Nine" on the creature packing list, but like many of the nicknames given by the crew, it was changed for marketing purposes.<ref name="SW Interviews">{{Blogspot|subdomain=starwarsinterviews1|url=2010/01/mike-quinn-interview.html|name=Star Wars Interviews|text=Mike Quinn Interview}}</ref>

Nunb was voiced by [[Kipsang Rotich]], a student from [[Wikipedia:Kenya|Kenya]], in his native tongue of [[Wikipedia:Haya language|Haya]]. In the movie, Nunb can also be heard speaking [[Wikipedia:Gikuyu language|Kikuyu]], another Kenyan language.<ref name="Kenya">{{WebCite|url=https://www.csmonitor.com/1983/0728/072823.html|text=In Kenya, audiences roar at language in 'Jedi' film|date=1983-07-28|archivedate=20190811180657}}</ref>

Nien Nunb has been used as a gag in several modern cartoons including ''Family Guy'' and ''The Venture Bros''. He is also referred to as the "Pancake Kid" by [[Billy Dee Williams]] on [[Robot Chicken: Star Wars|''Robot Chicken'']].

In Fall [[2009]], Hasbro released a red B-Wing Pilot in the Legacy Collection [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']] Line. The figure was named 'Nien Nunb', implying that Nunb was originally the red-suited B-Wing Pilot who stood behind Lando Calrissian in the pre-Endor Briefing Room, and that Lando asked Nunb to be his co-pilot in the Falcon after the briefing. The figure uses the same mold as the Keyan Farlander B-Wing figure, and comes with his own helmet similar to [[Ten Numb/Legends|Ten Numb]] with a breathing apparatus attachment.
